slots.practicalActivity: Create a free Azure account (or sign in to an existing one), open 'Create a resource' in the Portal and search for 3 real services (e.g. Virtual Machines, App Service, Azure SQL Database), and classify each as IaaS, PaaS, or SaaS with a one-sentence justification for who manages what.
slots.deliverable: A 3-row IaaS/PaaS/SaaS classification table for 3 real Azure services, each with a one-sentence justification.

lessons.title: Azure Global Infrastructure: Regions & Availability Zones

slots.practicalActivity: In the Azure Portal, open the Regions page and find your nearest Azure region; check whether it has Availability Zones, and compare it to one other region on a different continent to see the difference in available zones and services.
slots.deliverable: A short note naming your nearest Azure region, its Availability Zone support, and one comparison region with a noted difference.

slots.practicalActivity: Open the Subscriptions blade in your own Azure Portal and record your subscription ID and offer type, then create a real resource group named rg-az900-practice in your nearest region and apply a tag Environment=Training to it.
slots.deliverable: A created resource group named rg-az900-practice tagged Environment=Training, plus your subscription ID and offer type recorded in a short note.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter practice for Cloud & Azure Concepts: without looking back at the lessons, write a one-paragraph definition of cloud computing in your own words, sketch the IaaS/PaaS/SaaS responsibility split as a table, and confirm in the Portal that you can locate your subscription, your rg-az900-practice resource group, and your nearest region's Availability Zone info unaided.
slots.deliverable: A one-paragraph cloud-computing definition, an IaaS/PaaS/SaaS responsibility table, and a note confirming you located your subscription, resource group, and region/AZ info without referring back to the lessons.

lessons.title: Azure Compute Overview: VMs & App Service

slots.practicalActivity: Inside rg-az900-practice, deploy a small storage account (Standard_LRS) through the Portal; separately, open the Create a Virtual Machine and Create an App Service wizards (without finishing either) far enough to compare what each one asks you to configure, and write down the one key difference that defines IaaS vs. PaaS for compute.
slots.deliverable: A deployed storage account inside rg-az900-practice, plus a written one-sentence comparison of what the VM wizard vs. the App Service wizard each requires you to manage.

slots.practicalActivity: Inside rg-az900-practice, deploy a virtual network with one subnet in the same region as your storage account, then open its Overview page to confirm it lives inside rg-az900-practice alongside your other resources.
slots.deliverable: A deployed virtual network with one subnet inside rg-az900-practice, confirmed via its Overview page.

slots.practicalActivity: Open Microsoft Entra ID and view the Users blade for your directory, noting how many users exist and what role you have; then open Azure Monitor, select the storage account you deployed, and chart its 'Used capacity' metric over the last 24 hours under Metrics.
slots.deliverable: A written note on what you found in Entra ID's Users blade, plus a screenshot or description of an Azure Monitor metrics chart for your storage account.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for Core Azure Services: for each of compute, storage, networking, identity, and monitoring, name the one real Azure resource or blade you deployed or inspected this chapter and explain in one sentence what problem it solves, then confirm all the resources you created still live under rg-az900-practice.
slots.deliverable: A 5-row table (Compute/Storage/Networking/Identity/Monitoring) naming the specific service used for each and what it solves, plus confirmation all resources are grouped under rg-az900-practice.

slots.practicalActivity: On rg-az900-practice, open Access control (IAM), review the Role assignments tab, and add yourself (or a test account) with the Reader role at the resource-group scope; confirm the assignment appears and explain in writing why Reader differs from Contributor or Owner.
slots.deliverable: A confirmed Reader role assignment on rg-az900-practice, plus a short written explanation of the Reader/Contributor/Owner distinction.

slots.practicalActivity: Open the Azure Pricing Calculator and build a monthly cost estimate for the storage account and virtual network you deployed in Chapter 2, then compare that estimate against the real current spend shown in Cost Management + Billing for your subscription.
slots.deliverable: A saved Pricing Calculator estimate for your Chapter 2 resources, plus a written comparison against your subscription's actual Cost Management figures.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a second tag (CostCenter=Training) to rg-az900-practice, then in Azure Policy's built-in definitions search for 'Require a tag on resource groups' and open its JSON to see exactly what it checks; separately, look up one real compliance certification Azure holds for your region via the Microsoft Trust Center and note which one applies.
slots.deliverable: A resource group with two tags applied, written notes on what the built-in tag-requirement policy's JSON checks, and one named real compliance certification relevant to your region.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter review for Security, Pricing & Governance: write a short governance plan (5-8 sentences) for a hypothetical company with 3 resource groups, specifying which tags you'd require, who gets Owner vs. Reader access, and what budget alert thresholds you'd set in Cost Management.
slots.deliverable: A written governance plan covering required tags, RBAC role assignments, and Cost Management budget alert thresholds for a hypothetical 3-resource-group subscription.

slots.practicalActivity: Open Azure Cloud Shell (or install the Azure CLI locally), run az login and az account show to confirm your subscription, then run az group list --output table to list your real resource groups from the command line, including rg-az900-practice.
slots.deliverable: A Cloud Shell/CLI session transcript showing az account show and az group list output, with rg-az900-practice visible in the results.

slots.practicalActivity: Open rg-az900-practice in the Portal and use Export template to download its real ARM template JSON, then identify the resources and tags sections inside it and compare the file's length and readability against what a Bicep version of the same resource group would look like.
slots.deliverable: A saved exported ARM template JSON from rg-az900-practice with the resources and tags sections identified in a written note.

slots.practicalActivity: Deploy a second storage account into rg-az900-practice twice: once through the Portal, once via az storage account create from the CLI, confirming both succeed and appear side by side using az resource list --resource-group rg-az900-practice --output table.
slots.deliverable: Two successfully deployed storage accounts in rg-az900-practice (one via Portal, one via CLI), confirmed together in one az resource list output.

slots.practicalActivity: Review the AZ-900 exam's published skills-measured outline (Cloud Concepts / Azure Architecture & Services / Management & Governance), map each domain to the chapter of this course that covered it, and take a free official Microsoft Learn AZ-900 practice assessment to identify your weakest domain.
slots.deliverable: A mapping of each AZ-900 exam domain to the covering chapter, plus an AZ-900 practice-assessment score with your weakest domain named.

slots.practicalActivity: Final course lab: delete rg-az900-practice entirely (az group delete --name rg-az900-practice --yes, or the Portal's Delete resource group button) to confirm every resource you deployed this course is torn down and billing stops; then retake the AZ-900 practice assessment and map your 2 weakest questions back to the specific lesson of this course that covered them.
slots.deliverable: Confirmation that rg-az900-practice and everything inside it was deleted, plus a second AZ-900 practice-assessment score with your 2 weakest questions mapped to the covering lesson.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can explain core cloud and Azure concepts, navigate the Azure Portal and CLI, and deploy, tag, secure, cost-estimate, and tear down basic Azure resources — the AZ-900-level foundation the rest of the DevOps Engineer path's Azure-flavored work builds on.
